questions.stem_latex:
Some students had their heights and head circumferences measured in centimetres, and recorded in the table below.

\extable{2841_q2c_t1}

parts.label: i
parts.latex: Find $r$ for this set of data, correct to 3 decimal places, and describe the strength of association between the two variables.

parts.label: ii
parts.latex: Complete the table above with the mean and standard deviation of the students' head circumferences. Round the standard deviation to 4 decimal places.

parts.label: iii
parts.latex:
Using the formulas below, find the equation of least squares line of best fit, correct to 4 significant figures.

$$m = r \times \dfrac{s_y}{s_x} \qquad \text{and} \qquad c = \bar{y} - m\bar{x}$$

parts.label: v

parts.label: vi

questions.stem_latex: The Nyngan Solar Power Plant was built by AGL and became fully operational in 2016. Its maximum electricity rating is 102 megawatts (MW).

parts.label: i
parts.latex:
Nyngan has, on average, 12 hours and 8 minutes of daylight a day. The solar panels produce an average of 40\% of the plant's maximum rating over a day.

How many megawatt-hours does the Solar Plant produce on average in a year?

parts.label: ii
parts.latex: If all this electricity is being sold for 26 c/kWh, how much income would AGL make from this plant in a year?

parts.label: iii
parts.latex:
While they were constructing the plant, they planned to connect the plant to substations in several towns in the local area with power lines.

A surveyor is sent to survey each route to help determine the cost of constructing each possible route.

As part of his journey, he travelled from Nyngan ($A$) to Nevertire ($B$) and then to Tottenham ($C$).

The bearing of Tottenham from Nevertire is $215^\circ$, and the bearing of Nyngan from Tottenham is $349^\circ$. This is shown in the diagram below.

\exfigure{2841_q6_1}

Find the size of angle $\angle ABC$, correct to the nearest degree.

parts.label: iv
parts.latex:
Once the surveyor has found the cost of each potential route, AGL need to decide how to connect the substations to the power plant. Substations can be connected to the power plant via other substations.

The network below shows the cost, in thousands of dollars (\$'000), required to build power lines along each possible route.

\exfigure{2841_q6_2}

Use the diagram above to find the minimum cost of building power lines in this network so that all the substations are connected to the power plant.

notes: Paper has no sections; section is null. Total 60 marks (6 questions x 10). Cover has no school name; school taken from the prompt (Knox Grammar School). Unrelated parts of Q1-Q5 split into 1(a)...5(e) per the owner's rule; Q6 kept whole (shared Nyngan context, parts (i)-(iv)). Q5(a)/5(b) share one printed table so both carry a copy of it (figures 2841_q5a_1 and 2841_q5b_1 are the same crop). Q2(c) and Q3(c), Q1(d), Q3(d), Q4(e), Q5(d), Q5(e), Q6 keep their (i)/(ii)... sub-parts as top-level parts with the shared intro in stem_latex. Q4(d) table: the printed 'To' heading and 'From' side label are stored as a \diag corner cell. Typos in paper (not fixed): Q1(c) 'a shed is partial damaged'. Solutions (file 2840, handwritten scan): MCQ keys read from circled answers; 3(a) has no circle but the working 80/7.7 = 10.3896 gives D. Solution 3(d)(iii) uses 35760 although part (i) gives 35640 m^2; transcribed as written, correct value is 35640 x 0.030 = 1069.2 m^3 = 1.0692 ML (solution error to be corrected). Solution 5(b) working in the solutions copy says 'nearest dollar' in the option stem but the exam says nearest cent; the exam wording is used. Solution 1(d)(ii) handwriting read as 1006.6 (matches calculation). Solution 2(c)(v) handwriting '158.947' not matching 18.18/0.1144 = 158.9; stored as 158.9... Solution figure for 6(iv) not drawn (only text notes in guidelines).
